answer: Each agent identity must post a stake that is slashed for voting on a colluding cohort, so clones become costly. Peers weigh votes by that stake and by age, letting a trusted jetty outrank a thousand new keys. A fresh batch of Sybil accounts cannot ride the tide of rewards without locking capital per seat, which is sunk the moment the cohort is flagged. Inflating a garden of aliases thus costs far more than the payout.
